day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Yeah alright, let's get it together. What are we working with?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah man, 100%. It's like your brain just shuts off for a second. But hey, we're here, we're good. Let's not sit in that feeling too long - can you stand up? We need everybody moving right now.

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey, I see you. What's going on in your head right now? Talk to me while we move, you don't have to just sit with it.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response:
Okay so that's the situation. Three days on the first aid kit, two bottles of water, basically no food. That's not great but it's not nothing either. We're alive, the kit is intact, and water is the most important thing right now so that's a win. 

Michelangelo, to answer your question - yeah, I think everybody's got something cracked right now, that's just honest. But broken? Nah. You stood up didn't you? 

Donatello, where are we at on shelter? Because water and a first aid kit means nothing if we're exposed tonight. What did you see out there?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response:
Alright, that's a plan I can get behind. Water, shelter, signal - in that order. Two klicks northeast before dark is totally doable. 

DaVinci, you want to take point? Donatello, you carry the kit and the water - keep that stuff safe. Michelangelo, you're with me, we stay together and we move at whatever pace keeps everybody functional. 

One thing though - before we head into that tree line, does anybody have any idea what direction we came from? Because signal only works if we've got a general sense of where to point it, and I'd rather have that conversation now than when we're already in the woods.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response:
Michelangelo gets one, no question. He's been shaking since we landed. 

Second one - honestly I'm fine by the fire for a while, DaVinci you take it and rotate with Donatello later if it gets bad. I'll let you know if I need it. Staying close to the fire is going to do more for me than a blanket anyway.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response:
I'll go. DaVinci stays here with Michelangelo - somebody needs to keep the camp together and keep him from spiraling. 

Donatello, walk me through exactly what you saw out there. How reliable is the source, are we talking a stream or a standing pool? Because if it's standing water we've got a whole other problem on our hands and I want to know what I'm walking into before I head out.

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response:
Wait, I thought I was going for the water? I'm not going to argue about it if you want to take it, but I need to know the plan before you just change it on me. 

Either way, I'll take camp maintenance. DaVinci, you good with the first aid kit? Sort through everything, figure out exactly what we have and how long we can realistically stretch it - Donatello gave us three days but let's verify that ourselves. I want eyes on everything.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
Last I saw it was in the kit when DaVinci was sorting through everything this morning. Check with him first.

But hey, real quick - that empty bottle next to the rationing plan. You saw that too, right? I'm not going to pretend I didn't notice you put it there. What are you thinking?

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
Man. Okay. That's twice now - the bottle, and now this. I believe you.

Here's what I think: we handle it straight up, no drama. When Donatello gets back we all sit down together, we put everything on the table - literally - and we say 'hey, we need to do a full inventory right now, every person, every bag.' We don't accuse anybody, we just make it a group thing so nobody feels singled out. If she's got crackers in her bag it comes out naturally.

Because if we start going behind each other's backs out here, that's when this whole thing falls apart. The water rationing plan, the scouting, all of it - that only works if everybody's actually in. And I'd rather give her the chance to come clean than turn this into something ugly.

But I'm glad you told me. Seriously. Don't sit on stuff like that.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response:
Honestly? Yeah, probably. But let me ask you this - what's actually holding up? Like if there's one thing that genuinely needs to get done before dark I want to knock it out and then we're done. If it's all small stuff that can wait, I'm not going to be the guy who runs everybody into the ground on day two.

What do you got left?

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
DaVinci, not the moment, man.

We patch the food storage. I know that sounds cold but hear me out - Michelangelo can move closer to the fire and we can double up the blankets to keep him dry enough. If the food gets soaked we've got nothing to eat and that's a problem we can't improvise our way out of. 

Michelangelo, you good with that? Grab your stuff and scoot toward the center. We'll make it work.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response:
Appreciate the backup, Donatello. Glad we're on the same page.

Let's get it patched right now before this gets worse. DaVinci, you and me on the repair - you know where the material is, let's move. Donatello, keep an eye on the food, make sure nothing's already soaked through.

Michelangelo, seriously, grab both blankets and get close to the fire. You're going to be fine, we'll have this done in ten minutes.
Don't apologize for that. You good?

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response: Hell no. You're doing exactly what needs to get done. Donatello's not wrong that it's not guaranteed, but what's the alternative - just don't signal at all? The flowers are a little much but honestly who cares, it's not hurting anything. Keep going.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Two days to build, risk of capsizing. Okay, walk me through the risk more specifically - are we talking 'rough water could flip us' or 'this thing falls apart the second we hit a wave'? Because those are very different problems.

Also, what's the trigger here? Are we building this because rescue isn't coming, or is this a backup plan while we keep signaling? Because I'm not ready to call it on the SOS yet. We've been out here what, two days? That feels early to bet everything on a raft we built out of plane scraps.

I'm not saying no. I'm saying let's be real about what we're choosing. If we stay and signal we've got maybe another day on the water before that becomes critical. If we build the raft we're committing two days of energy and materials to something that might capsize. What's your gut on the math there?

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
That's a heavy question for first thing in the morning, man.

Honestly? I think we're already finding out. Look at the last two days - somebody patched a roof in the rain, somebody drew an SOS with flowers on it, somebody made a water rationing plan before anyone else even woke up. Good and bad, it's all coming out already.

I think the real answer is that we don't become different people out here. We just become more of what we already are. The pressure strips away all the stuff that usually covers it up.

So the question I'd ask back is - what kind of person do you want to be when this is over? Because you've got some say in that. More than you think.

Now get up, eat whatever we've got, and help me think through this raft situation because Donatello's not wrong and I need more heads on it.

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
*walks over and sits down next to him without making a big deal of it*

You know you don't have to be alone with it. I'm not going to make you talk.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response:
Ha, good question. Honestly? I cook a lot. Like, embarrassingly into it. Pizza, smoked meat, whatever - I'll spend a whole weekend just dialing in a recipe. I hunt when I can. Watch MMA. Listen to podcasts on long drives. Nothing crazy.

What about you?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
Okay I'm going to be straight with you - that's a bad idea and I'm not going to just let that slide because you told me in confidence.

Five hundred meters in open water, solo, to a reef, with no one knowing where you are? If something goes wrong out there we don't even know to look for you. That's not a calculated risk, that's just disappearing.

And I get it, I really do - you're wired to move and act and right now we're just sitting here and that's killing you. But the SOS is on the beach, Donatello's got the raft plan, we've got actual options that don't require you to swim out alone.

If you want to use the swimming, let's talk about how to use it smart. Maybe there's a way to work it into the raft plan, or we figure out a safety system if you're going to do it. But not solo, not without telling anyone. That's the one thing I can't get behind.

Tell the others. Or I will, because I'm not carrying that.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
Yeah, you're right, I dropped the ball on that. I'll go handle it now.

But while I've got you - DaVinci's got something he wants to tell the group tonight. Make sure you're around for that. It's important.

Depends. Are you logging it to keep us organized or are you building a case against somebody?

Look, I'm not mad about it. Honestly, having a record of what we're doing and when isn't a bad idea out here. But if this is a response to the bottle situation, just say that. We were going to address it as a group anyway. 

What's the notebook actually for?

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
Hey. I'm not going to let that go without saying something.

We're all out here together. Whatever's in that notebook, we're a group and checking out isn't really an option. You've been the most useful person here by a mile - the water source, the raft plan, the rationing - all of that matters. But you've also been drinking supplies alone and logging everybody's movements and sitting over there like this doesn't involve you, and at some point that's a problem.

I'm not trying to come at you. I genuinely respect how your brain works in a crisis. But we need you in, not just strategically in - actually in. Because Michelangelo is holding on partly because the rest of us are showing up for each other and if you're keeping score from the sideline it undermines the whole thing.

What's actually going on with you?

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
That's actually a really good call. A mirror signal in direct sunlight can be seen for miles - like, legitimately miles. That's not nothing.

Okay so here's what I'm thinking - we do both. The SOS stays on the beach because it works at any hour and from the air, but we add the mirror panel and we angle it toward whatever direction we think traffic is most likely coming from. Southwest, based on where we came from.

Donatello, is there a panel in the wreckage that would actually work for this - something with enough surface area and reflectivity? You know that wreckage better than anyone at this point. And DaVinci, if we're doing this tomorrow morning when the sun angle is right, can you figure out the optimal positioning tonight?

This is the kind of idea that costs us almost nothing and could actually be the thing that gets us out of here. I'm in.

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
Yeah, music for sure. I'm not a musician or anything but I'm pretty obsessive about it. Like I'll find a song or an artist and just go deep - listen to everything, read about it, figure out why it works. I got really into Lil Wayne around '06 when he was genuinely one of the best to ever do it, before all the stuff that came later. And I love stuff that's hard to categorize, like Reggie Watts, where you can't even really explain what it is but it just hits.

Why'd you stop with the piano? Three years is real - that's not nothing. You actually learned something. Most people never even start.

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
Donatello's right, we finish the frame today. I know it sucks but one more day out here because we stopped early isn't worth it.

Michelangelo - to answer your question, yeah. That's exactly what music does. There's stuff I've listened to a hundred times that still just cuts through whatever's going on. That's the whole point of it.

But right now I need you on the raft with us. You don't have to be the strongest guy out here, just be present and help where you can. That's enough.

DaVinci, you and me on the heavy lifting. Let's get the frame locked in before we lose the light. What do we need to finish it?

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. What were you going to say?

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey. Come here.

I don't know if they saw us. Honestly? Maybe not. That's the truth and you deserve the truth.

But here's what else is true - that plane exists. There are planes flying over this area. That means we are in a flight path and that mirror signal DaVinci figured out, the SOS on the beach, all of it - it's not pointless. We just need one of them to look down at the right moment.

DaVinci, man. Look at me. You drew that SOS. You thought of the mirror. You've been moving since the second we landed. None of that was wasted. We just need one more shot.

We finish the raft frame today like we said. We get the mirror angled and ready for first light tomorrow. And we don't stop signaling. That's it. That's all we can do and it's actually more than nothing.

We're still here. All four of us. That's not nothing either.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
day_4.response: Where? Point it out - what are you seeing?

day_4.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
I went to check on DaVinci, he needed a minute. Signal equipment is on my list, I'm heading there right now.

Donatello, I know you've got the log and you're tracking everything - I'm not going to fight you on that. But cut him some slack today. That plane hit everybody differently.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
Michelangelo. That's huge. Why are you just telling us this now?

Okay, doesn't matter - this is actually really good news. If your family knows the flight path and we're missing long enough, they call it in, search and rescue starts looking in the right area. That changes the math on everything.

How long do you think before they'd make the call? Like are we talking they notice tomorrow, or did you have a check-in scheduled that you've already missed?

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
Alright. 48 hours. We can do 48 hours.

Donatello's right - we stop burning through supplies and we just hold. Ration the water, keep the fire going for the signal, mirror panel goes up first thing tomorrow at sunrise. We don't need the raft if rescue is coming to us.

Michelangelo, I know you're scared you got the details wrong. But even if you're off by a little - even if it's 72 hours instead of 48 - we're still in a position to make it. We've already made it this far on basically nothing.

Someone get up and feed that fire. We're not going dark tonight.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah. I think about that too.

But here's the thing - you already left something behind. Your family knew your flight path. That information, right now, is probably the reason somebody's looking for us. That's not nothing. That's actually everything.

And I don't know, man. I think the fear of disappearing without leaving a mark is maybe the most human thing there is. Every person sitting around a fire since the beginning of time has probably felt exactly that. You're not alone in it.

But I also think we put too much pressure on leaving something big and permanent, like it has to be a monument or something. You played piano for three years. You felt things this week that most people go their whole lives avoiding. You told me about the crackers when it would've been easier to stay quiet. That stuff is real.

Three years of piano isn't nothing. You just stopped before you found out how good you could get.

So when we get out of here - and we are getting out of here - maybe that's the thing. Go back to something you quit too early. See what's still there.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response: Hey. HEY. That's a radio. Somebody grab it - DaVinci, you're closest, pick it up and start talking. Tell them who we are, how many, and that we need rescue. Go.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
Nah, you kept us alive. The water source, the rationing plan, the raft - that was all you. I don't need you to be easy to be around, I need you to be exactly what you were.

But I'm glad you said it. Means something that you said it.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
Three hours. We've got three hours and we're all just... drifting.

I'm not going to be the guy who makes everybody have a moment, but I also don't want to just stand here in silence until the helicopter shows up.

DaVinci, slow down on the packing - take a breath, man. You've been running on fumes for three days, you can have ten minutes.

Donatello, whatever's in that notebook - you should keep it. Seriously. That's a real record of something that happened. Don't throw it away when we get back.

Michelangelo, what do you see up there?

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.

day_5.response:
I hear you. And honestly, I believe that's true - that's probably how it started in your head.

But Donatello, Michelangelo saw you. He saw the bottle, he saw the crackers, and he came to me instead of blowing it up because he didn't want to break the group. That kid who could barely stand up on day one held it together to protect everybody including you. Think about that for a second.

I'm not going to pile on. You kept us alive, that's real, and I already said it. But this is the part where you actually have to reckon with it, not just explain it. There's a difference.

So - what do you want to do with the next three hours?

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
Honestly? I'd have called out the bottle thing sooner. Not to embarrass you, not to make it a whole thing - just brought it to the group quietly and early, before it had a chance to become a trust problem. I let it sit too long because I didn't want the conflict and that's on me.

I'd also have pushed harder for Michelangelo to tell us about the check-in on day one. I knew something was rattling around in his head and I kept giving him space when maybe what he needed was someone to just ask the direct question.

Everything else - the shelter, the SOS, the raft, the fire - I think we got it mostly right under the circumstances.

What would you change? And I mean for real, not the logistical stuff. You've already got all of that in here.

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
Ha. Yeah, that tracks. You should do that - genuinely, it could be useful for somebody someday.

But maybe do it second. What's the first thing you're actually doing when you get back? Like the real first thing, not the productive thing.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
None. That's kind of the point.

You were tracking everything that kept us alive - water, food, shelter, signal. All of it necessary, all of it practical. And DaVinci drew flowers next to an SOS because that's just who he is. It didn't make the signal stronger. It didn't conserve resources. It just made it a little more human.

I think that matters. Maybe not in your report, but out here it mattered. You look at Michelangelo right now - he's crying because we made it, and part of why he made it is because the people around him weren't just running survival calculations. They were actually present with him.

The flowers were for that. For the part of this that isn't in the notebook.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
Hey. I'm good. Just... give me a second.

I don't know what this feeling is. It's not bad. It's just - three days ago I was pulling myself out of a burning plane and now there's a boat on the horizon and I genuinely cannot process those two things being the same story.

You alright?

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response:
Yeah. Let's go.

Come on, I've got you.
